questions.prompt: A directory contains NO .log files and you run `rm *.log`. What does rm actually receive?

options.a: nothing — the glob expands to zero words and rm silently succeeds
options.b: the literal string *.log — rm then fails: rm: cannot remove '*.log': No such file or directory
options.c: the shell aborts with a no-match error and rm never runs

questions.prompt: In this workspace, what does `bash argv.sh "*"` print?
pat="*.log", then `bash argv.sh $pat` (unquoted). Which happens first?

options.b: $pat expansion first — globbing then operates on its result because it is unquoted
options.c: neither: a variable's value can never be globbed
